name: Atit Agarwal
current_role: Former Non-Executive Chairman, Responsive Industries Ltd (Mumbai) - chairmanship ended 2018; current role not confirmed
profile: Atit Omprakash Agarwal is a member of the Agarwal family that owns and manages Responsive Industries, a BSE/NSE-listed Mumbai maker of PVC/vinyl, SPC and LVT flooring, synthetic leather and (via Axiom Cordages) ropes. He chaired the company until 2018; the family business has since been fronted by Rishabh Agarwal.
interesting_fact: Responsive Industries describes itself as India's No.1 LVP/SPC flooring maker, with plants in India, Vietnam and Thailand exporting to 70+ countries; the family moved from ropes into PVC flooring in the early 1990s.
notes: Low public profile; little press coverage of Atit personally. Insider profiles (MarketScreener) show chairmanship ending 2018-09-30. Company contacts are corporate, not personal. Best route probably via company office or Rishabh Agarwal.

name: Sat Paul Singhla
current_role: Founder & Managing Director, S P Singla Constructions / SPS Construction India Pvt Ltd
profile: Sat Paul Singla (also spelled Singhla) is a civil engineer and first-generation entrepreneur who founded S P Singla Constructions in 1996 with no capital. The privately held firm specialises in river bridges, highways and metro work across ~15 Indian states and reported revenue of Rs 1,150 crore in FY2017, while remaining fully owned by him.
interesting_fact: His company built what it calls India's longest cable-stayed bridge, between Okha and Beyt Dwarka in Gujarat, plus an extradosed bridge across the Ganges between Aunta and Simaria in Bihar.
deep_cut_fact: Before starting out on his own he spent 12 years with small construction firms in Punjab and Haryana building river bridges in J&K, Punjab and Himachal; his first project as an entrepreneur was a small bridge over the Yamuna in 1996 worth just Rs 10 lakh.
notes: Private company, low media profile; Forbes India 'Built To Last' profile is the main press source. Registered office New Delhi, corporate office Panchkula (Haryana). Alive status not confirmed by a recent source.

name: Samit Satish Mehta
current_role: Executive Director (Operations), Emcure Pharmaceuticals; Whole-Time Director & CEO, Gennova Biopharmaceuticals
profile: Samit Mehta is the son of Emcure founder Satish Mehta and a whole-time director of the Pune-based drugmaker, which listed on Indian exchanges in 2024. He built Emcure's business in regulated markets (US, EU, Canada) and in July 2026 was named to lead Gennova, its now wholly owned biologics/mRNA subsidiary.
interesting_fact: Gennova developed India's first mRNA COVID-19 vaccine (HGCO19), designed to be stable at 2-8 degrees C; Mehta argued emerging markets would not adopt a vaccine needing a sub-zero cold chain.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family business he worked as a strategy management consultant at Ernst & Young in India.
notes: Gennova also works on saRNA vaccines (e.g. Nipah) - good biotech/manufacturing angle. Emcure's site blocks automated fetches; IR email taken from earnings-call transcript.

name: Jennifer Lawrence
current_role: Actor; co-founder of production company Excellent Cadaver
profile: Oscar-winning American actor (Silver Linings Playbook) from Louisville, Kentucky, best known for The Hunger Games and X-Men films. Her wealth comes from acting fees; since 2018 she has produced through Excellent Cadaver with partner Justine Ciarrocchi (Causeway, No Hard Feelings, Die My Love, 2025).
interesting_fact: In 2025 she received the San Sebastian festival's Donostia Award, becoming its youngest-ever recipient; Martin Scorsese sent her company the novel behind Die My Love and is re-teaming with her on What Happens at Night.
deep_cut_fact: She left school at 14 and calls herself 'self-educated'; between early acting jobs she worked as an assistant nurse at the children's summer camp her mother managed in Kentucky.
notes: Wealth is entertainment income; weak fit for the podcast. No personal social media. Board member of anti-corruption nonprofit RepresentUs; her foundation funded a cardiac ICU at Kosair Children's Hospital (2016). Approach via her agency/publicist (none found published) or Excellent Cadaver.

name: Mark Newcomer
current_role: President, CEO & Co-founder, Paysign, Inc. (NASDAQ: PAYS), Henderson, Nevada
profile: Mark Newcomer co-founded Paysign (formerly 3PEA) in 2001 and has run it since, taking it from an early prepaid-card issuer processor to a NASDAQ-listed (2018) payments and software platform. It leads U.S. plasma-donor compensation cards and pharma co-pay programs, and in 2025 expanded into SaaS for the blood/plasma industry (Apherion).
interesting_fact: Under Newcomer, Paysign built a market-leading position paying U.S. plasma donors via prepaid cards, then bought software that became the Apherion donor-management ecosystem for blood and plasma centers.
deep_cut_fact: He studied bioscience at Cal Poly San Luis Obispo, a background he credits for his interest in platforms for complex, regulated healthcare markets.
notes: Stepped down as chairman in 2025 (Dan Henry became chair), remains CEO. Fintech/healthcare angle rather than energy. Press releases also list ir@paysign.com.

name: Patricia K Poppe
profile: Patti Poppe, a Purdue industrial engineer, spent ~15 years at General Motors before moving to DTE Energy (2005) and Consumers Energy (2011), becoming its CEO. Since 2021 she has led PG&E, California's largest utility, through post-bankruptcy wildfire-safety work and grid buildout, including data-center load growth.
interesting_fact: She is described as the first woman to be CEO of two Fortune 500 companies (CMS Energy/Consumers Energy and PG&E).
deep_cut_fact: At GM she turned down a promotion that came with a company car to become a second-shift trim-shop supervisor, which she calls the second-hardest job she's had: 'Take the tough jobs where you're going to learn the core business.'
notes: Excellent fit for energy/data-center podcast (PG&E has a large data-center interconnection queue). Business Roundtable member; inducted into Automotive Hall of Fame. Media relations line published on PG&E pages: 415-973-5930. Approach via PG&E corporate communications.

name: Carolyn Rafaelian
current_role: Founder, Metal Alchemist and Alchemist Mint; steward of Belcourt (Newport, R.I.)
profile: Rhode Island jewelry entrepreneur who founded bangle brand Alex and Ani in 2004 and became a billionaire before the company's decline and her 2020 exit. She relaunched with Metal Alchemist (2022), jewelry forged entirely in Rhode Island, and in 2026 started Alchemist Mint, selling commemorative coins made from original Statue of Liberty copper.
interesting_fact: She owns Belcourt, a 56,000-sq-ft Gilded Age Newport mansion designed by Richard Morris Hunt (architect of the Statue of Liberty's pedestal), where a permanent Statue of Liberty metals exhibition opened in June 2026.
deep_cut_fact: In 2016 she took custody of copper salvaged in the 1984-86 Statue of Liberty restoration at the request of collector Rick Stocks, whose wish was 'to get Lady Liberty off her pedestal and make her available to the public.'
notes: Avoid Alex and Ani loan default/firing topics. Metal Alchemist and Belcourt channels are brand accounts, not personal. Also founded &Livy. Forbes notes she has a priest and shaman bless inventory - leans into 'positive energy' branding.

name: Ryan H. Saadi
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Tevogen Bio Holdings (NASDAQ: TVGN)
profile: Dr. Ryan Saadi, MD, MPH, spent nearly three decades in hospital administration, managed care and life-sciences leadership before founding Tevogen Bio in 2020, which went public via SPAC in 2024. Tevogen develops off-the-shelf allogeneic precision T-cell therapies (virology, oncology, neurology); he controls a majority of the voting stock.
interesting_fact: Tevogen board member Curtis Patton (Yale School of Public Health) nominated Saadi and Tevogen for the 2023 Nobel Peace Prize for a business model aimed at making T-cell therapy affordable.
deep_cut_fact: He was a 2019 PharmaVoice 'Red Jacket' honoree for challenging the status quo on equal access to healthcare; his motto for Tevogen is 'doing well by doing good.'
notes: Named to 2025 NJBIZ Power 100. Tevogen also runs an AI unit (Tevogen.AI) - possible data/AI angle. Social links are company accounts.

name: Robert C Pohlad
current_role: President & CEO, Pohlad Holdings (Dakota Holdings); independent director, PepsiCo
profile: Bob Pohlad, son of financier Carl Pohlad, has led the family's Pohlad Holdings since 1987 (real estate, automation/robotics, sports & entertainment) and was Chairman & CEO of PepsiAmericas until PepsiCo bought it in 2010. The family has owned the Minnesota Twins since 1984; he has been a PepsiCo director since 2015.
interesting_fact: PepsiAmericas, formed in 1998 from several independent bottlers, grew under his leadership into the second-largest bottler of PepsiCo products before PepsiCo bought it in 2010.
deep_cut_fact: He chaired the University of Puget Sound Board of Trustees (signing its board reports as chair in 2018-2021), and was elected to Minnesota Public Radio's board of trustees in 2013.
notes: Arizona State grad (1976). Pohlad Holdings includes automation/robotics engineering businesses - possible industrial angle. Brothers Jim (Twins) and Bill (film producer) share equal ownership. No published personal contact; route via Pohlad Companies (Minneapolis) or PepsiCo corporate secretary.

name: Serge Saxonov
profile: Serge Saxonov co-founded 10x Genomics in 2012 with Ben Hindson and Kevin Ness and has been CEO since inception, building it into a leader in single-cell and spatial biology instruments. Earlier he was 23andMe's first employee (founding architect, director of R&D) and VP of applications at droplet-digital-PCR startup QuantaLife, sold to Bio-Rad in 2011 for $162m.
interesting_fact: He was 23andMe's first employee, helping define the consumer genetics company's original product concept; Goldman Sachs named him one of its 100 Most Intriguing Entrepreneurs in 2016.
deep_cut_fact: Born in the former Soviet Union, he emigrated to the US as a teenager, went to Bronx Science, then studied at Harvard under genomics pioneer and Nobel laureate Wally Gilbert before a Stanford PhD in biomedical informatics.
notes: Good fit for data/compute angle: 10x is pushing AI-scale biological datasets (e.g. Cancer Research Institute AI immuno-oncology initiative, 2026). Has appeared on GEN's 'Close to the Edge' podcast.

name: Jonathan M Heller
current_role: CEO, Helix Partners Management LP; Trustee, Office Properties Income Trust (since June 2026)
profile: Jonathan Heller is a distressed/credit investor who runs Helix Partners Management, which became a 10%+ holder of Office Properties Income Trust in 2026 alongside his board seat. Previously a partner overseeing Canyon Partners' New York office, he chaired mall REIT CBL Properties after its 2021 restructuring until stepping down in January 2023 to build Helix.
interesting_fact: He became chairman of CBL Properties within weeks of joining its board in late 2021, steering the mall owner after it emerged from Chapter 11.
notes: Low public profile. Background per aggregator profiles: Yeshiva University undergrad, began as an accountant at PwC (unverified by primary source). helixpartners.com appears to be his credit-focused firm (matches 'Helix Partners'), but site does not name him - verify before use. OPI holdings via Helix Strategic Fund I/II per June 2026 Form 3.

name: Edward Urban Kissel
current_role: Managing Partner & Portfolio Manager, Forager Capital Management (Birmingham, Alabama)
profile: Ed Kissel co-runs Forager Capital Management with Robert MacArthur, a Birmingham, Alabama manager of concentrated small-cap public equity and private equity funds (about $353m AUM). Through Forager Fund, L.P. the firm has filed as a 10%+ owner of MasterCraft Boat Holdings and consumer lender Regional Management.
interesting_fact: Forager is a small Birmingham, Alabama shop (about 3 staff, ~$353m AUM) that has nonetheless filed as a 10%+ holder of two U.S.-listed companies, MasterCraft and Regional Management.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding Forager he was an analyst at Fidelity (2010-2011), after graduating from the University of Pennsylvania in 2008.
notes: Very low public profile; career details from aggregator (MarketScreener), not primary source. Firm SEC-registered 2021 (CRD 158835). MasterCraft announced a 2026 merger with Marine Products Corp. Weak fit for energy/data-center podcast.

name: Paul Ahlstrom
current_role: Co-founder & Managing Director, Alta Ventures Mexico; Director, Angel Studios (NYSE: ANGX)
profile: Utah entrepreneur and VC (BYU grad) who founded software firm Knowlix, then co-founded vSpring Capital (2000), Alta Growth Capital and Kickstart Seed Fund (2007) and Monterrey-based Alta Ventures Mexico (2010), helping manage $1bn+ across 150+ companies. Alta backed Provo's Angel Studios, where he is a director.
interesting_fact: He is co-author of the startup methodology book 'Nail It Then Scale It' and its Big Idea Canvas, and lists 'disrupting Hollywood, ending poverty, curing cancer' as missions he invests behind.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming a VC he was founder and CEO of Knowlix, a knowledge-management software company that raised venture funding in 1998; he sold his last tech company before launching vSpring in 2000.
notes: Member of Utah Angels; based in Provo, UT. Angel Studios went public via reverse merger in Sept 2025. No published personal contact found; Alta Ventures Mexico or Angel Studios IR are the likely routes. Good entrepreneurship-podcast fit (frequent speaker).

name: Sierk Poetting
current_role: Chief Operating Officer & Management Board member, BioNTech SE; Chairman of the Board, IQM (Finland)
profile: German physicist-turned-executive (b. 1973) who started at McKinsey, held finance roles at Novartis/Sandoz (CFO Sandoz North America 2012-14), then joined BioNTech in 2014 as CFO and later COO, helping scale the Mainz company through its COVID-19 vaccine with Pfizer. He also chairs IQM, a Finnish quantum-computer maker.
interesting_fact: He chairs the board of IQM Quantum Computers in Espoo, Finland - an unusual quantum-hardware role for a biotech COO.
deep_cut_fact: He did his physics PhD at the Max Planck Institute for Quantum Optics (thesis: 'Coherent momentum state manipulation of matter waves', 2004) after a University of Arizona MS thesis on 'Gap solitons in atomic Bose-Einstein condensates'.
notes: Strong compute angle via IQM quantum computing. BioNTech management board term listed as ending 2026 - check whether reappointed (BioNTech named a new CEO, Guido Oelkers, in 2026).

name: Aghili Naseem Sagati
current_role: Partner, General Counsel & Corporate Secretary, Ares Management Corporation
profile: Naseem Sagati Aghili joined alternative asset manager Ares in 2009 from Proskauer Rose (M&A, securities) and rose through roles including General Counsel of Private Equity and Co-General Counsel before becoming General Counsel in January 2020. She oversees Legal & Compliance plus enterprise risk, internal audit and performance functions.
interesting_fact: She became Ares' sole General Counsel in 2020 after co-leading the department with Michael Weiner, as Ares grew into one of the largest private-credit managers; Ares is now a major infrastructure and data-center financier.
deep_cut_fact: She studied 'Political Economy of Industrial Societies' at UC Berkeley before earning her JD at USC Gould School of Law.
notes: Lawyer/executive rather than founder; wealth from Ares equity. Some 2026 Ares releases use media@ares.com instead of aresmgmt.com. Pitch would be about private credit financing energy/digital infrastructure.

name: James F. Deutsch
current_role: Partner, Patriot Financial Partners, L.P.; Director, Midland States Bancorp (since Feb 2026)
profile: Jim Deutsch is a partner and investment-committee member at Patriot Financial Partners, a private equity fund focused on banks and financial services, through which he holds 10%+ of USCB Financial and a stake in Midland States Bancorp. He spent 25+ years in commercial banking, investment banking and corporate finance and founded Pennsylvania's Team Capital Bank.
interesting_fact: He joined Midland States' board on Feb 3, 2026, the same day the bank announced Patriot had built a position via open-market purchases - board expanded from 10 to 11 seats for him.
deep_cut_fact: Before private equity he was the founder, President and CEO of Team Capital Bank, a Pennsylvania community bank.
notes: Low public profile; bank-focused PE investor, weak fit for energy/data-center theme. USCB link comes from SEC insider data (Patriot as 10% owner). Route via Patriot Financial Partners (Philadelphia); no published direct contact found.

name: David E Rainbolt
current_role: Chairman, BancFirst Corporation (non-executive since Jan 2025); Director, OGE Energy Corp.
profile: David Rainbolt, son of BancFirst founder Gene Rainbolt, was CEO of the Oklahoma City bank holding company for 25 years from 1992, taking it public in 1993 and completing 34 acquisitions as assets grew from under $700m to over $7bn. He became chairman in 2017 and also sits on the board of utility OGE Energy.
interesting_fact: He was inducted into the Oklahoma Hall of Fame in 2018 and has chaired the Oklahoma City and Oklahoma State Chambers of Commerce, United Way of Central Oklahoma and the Dean McGee Eye Institute.
deep_cut_fact: He rode on the Shawnee High School rodeo team, and later coached his sons' little-league baseball teams for 24 years; he keeps a retreat on the Washita River near Tishomingo, where his ancestors settled in Indian Territory.
notes: Energy angle: OGE Energy board seat (Oklahoma utility seeing data-center load growth). Quote (2018): 'Oklahoma is too small and too poor to waste time with partisan fights over our scarce resources.' Started his career in Texas banking; moved back in 1982 to help modernize Oklahoma banking law.
